declaration: written before the run; every number in the report is produced by run_xval.py from the artefacts listed under environment
decision: Which elements of the lbmpy staged-gate CI practice (tag gitlab-ci-staged-gates in oss_solutions row 117) should TensorLBM adopt, and does TensorLBM's existing gate policy already deliver the same functional coverage (gated-corpus fraction) as the OSS policy?

alternatives.ALT-0: keep TensorLBM's flat GitHub Actions job set (baseline)
alternatives.ALT-1: transplant the GitLab ladder and its marker vocabulary verbatim
alternatives.ALT-2: transplant only what survives the KPI test: gate-tier taxonomy + declared-disabled-gate hygiene + coverage-report aggregation + an explicit marker-vocabulary adapter
alternatives.ALT-3: do nothing / declare the OSS practice irrelevant (rejected if any KPI shows a functional gap)

hypotheses.H1_functional_parity: On the default event (merge/pull request and non-default-branch push), the gated-corpus fraction of ALT-0 is within 15% of ALT-2 (the OSS policy evaluated on the same corpus with the vocabulary adapter).
hypotheses.H0_falsifier: |delta| >= 15% on guard_fraction or escape_fraction on any event/arm pair, or a simulator-fidelity error >= 15% on any validated selection expression.
hypotheses.H2_vocabulary_portability: The OSS marker expression (-m "not longrun") transplanted verbatim leaks >= 15% of this repository's long-tier tests into the fast gate, i.e. the vocabulary is repository-local and must be adapted, not copied.
hypotheses.H2_falsifier: verbatim leakage < 15% (the expression would be portable as-is).
hypotheses.H3_structural_only: The differences that remain after H1/H2 are structural (stage ladder, packaging of gates), not functional (what the gates inspect).

metrics.guard_fraction: |union of blocking+canditional gate selections over the corpus| / |corpus| on a given event (exact set arithmetic, host-independent)
metrics.long_tier_leakage: |{items marked 'slow'} INTERSECT fast-gate selection| / |{items marked 'slow'}| for a transplanted policy
metrics.n_blocking_gates: count of jobs with tier in {blocking, conditional} that are active on the event
metrics.ladder_declared_vs_active: declared stages vs stages that own at least one active job; declared-but-disabled job blocks
metrics.needs_edges: count of declared dependency edges between gates (the only mechanism that can serialise a ladder)
metrics.test_gate_configs: number of distinct (interpreter x backend) configurations the test gate runs on
metrics.artifact_contracts: number of declared artifact/report contracts (junit, coverage xml/html, html doc, pages)
metrics.simulator_fidelity: relative error between the simulator's selection size and the count pytest itself prints for the same -m expression
metrics.unit_of_analysis: one (policy, event) pair; the corpus snapshot is the fixed workload

baseline_control.baseline: ALT-0 = TensorLBM .github/workflows/ci.yml at the commit this branch was cut from
baseline_control.control: ALT-2 = the OSS policy with only the declarative vocabulary adapted, evaluated on the same corpus; the difference between ALT-1 and ALT-2 isolates the vocabulary port alone
baseline_control.workload: one pytest collection snapshot of TensorLBM (tests/ + app/tests), markers recorded per test id

predeclared_thresholds.parity_rule: H1 holds iff |guard_fraction(ALT-0) - guard_fraction(ALT-2)| < 15% for every event (relative to the OSS value)
predeclared_thresholds.leakage_rule: H2 holds iff verbatim leak >= 15% and adapted leak < 15%
predeclared_thresholds.fidelity_rule: simulator_fidelity rel. error < 15% for all validated expressions, else the simulator's KPIs are declared unvalidated and H1/H2 are withheld

stopping_rule: One deterministic evaluation per (arm, event); no arm is re-run or extended after inspecting the KPIs. The four validated expressions are fixed in advance: 'not slow', 'slow', 'unit', 'not longrun'. If the shared measurement host cannot finish the collection measurements within 30 min, the fidelity check is reported as incomplete (WITHHELD), not relaxed.
variables_controlled: test corpus snapshot (single collection, per-test marker sets)
marker expression semantics (pytest boolean rules, validated against pytest itself)
path scope of each gate (pytest path arguments / testpaths)
interpretation of tiers (blocking / advisory / conditional / manual, declared in ci_spec.py)
confounders: shared measurement host: load average 173 on 128 cores while collecting (co-tenant agent pytest runs) -> wall clock is NOT a criterion; only exact counts/set arithmetic are, and CPU time is reported for context
6 test modules fail to import in the control environment (stale editable install pointing at another worktree) -> they are absent from the corpus; declared corpus-completeness limitation
the OSS side is evaluated on TensorLBM's corpus, not on lbmpy's own tests: this is a single-workload policy comparison, not a comparison of the two code bases
the GitLab job `pages` is restricted by a branch-name condition (CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == master); the branch-name -> event mapping is a convention, not declared by GitLab

the nox session ids in CI are parametrized strings (testsuite-3.13(cpu)); they are resolved to session bodies by ast parsing, so a session rename upstream would silently degrade the OSS spec (guarded by tests)
repetition_rationale: All KPIs are deterministic functions of (spec, corpus, event): zero variance, so repetition adds nothing. Variation is supplied by 4 events x 4 arms + 4 independently measured selection expressions (simulator validation) + two marker-vocabulary arms (verbatim vs adapted).

environment.note: PYTHONPATH=src is required: the container's editable install points at another worktree, so the default import is the wrong tree
commands: PYTHONPATH=src python xval/gitlab_ci_staged_gates/measure_selections.py --exprs 'not slow' slow unit 'not longrun'

analysis_plan: For each (arm, event): guard_fraction, escape_fraction, gate inventory, ladder structure. Then (a) parity test H1 on the default events, (b) vocabulary leakage test H2 for ALT-1 vs ALT-2, (c) simulator fidelity against pytest's own counts for the four fixed expressions. Verdict -> chosen alternative. No threshold is changed after the run; every failure is reported as measured.
interpretation_limits: a policy KPI is not a defect-detection quality measure: guard_fraction says what a gate *inspects*, not what it would catch
wall-clock/cost differences between CI providers are not measured here (no CI runner access); the ladder's runtime effect is only reasoned about, never claimed as measured
H1 parity on coverage does not imply parity of gate *strictness* (timeouts, coverage thresholds, lint scope) - those are reported descriptively
